adaptations.description: Retains the judgments/functions/families/inductive types/identity sequence while separating Lambdapi conversion, proof-time comparison, and internal equality evidence.

Reworks the higher-groupoid, functions-as-functors, and families-as-fibrations themes into explicit iterated hom-categories, directed functors, Cat-valued families, total categories, and section categories.

Retains the propositions-as-types, mere propositions, sets, constructive logic, and contractibility progression while tying each implemented claim to emdash evidence and deferring truncation recursion to Chapter 7.
Uses the inverse-data-to-contractible-fibres progression, then separates type equivalence, ordinary categorical isomorphism, and recursive equality-valued omega-equivalence.
Compares the HoTT identity-to-equivalence and univalence interface with emdash groupoid, truncated-universe, and directed categorical equality boundaries without claiming one global univalence axiom.
Uses based identity induction as the groupoidal reference point for the explicit fixed-source outgoing-arrow induction construction.
Adapts the universal-property viewpoint to contextual categorical elimination while distinguishing the checked arrow-induction interface from unimplemented general homotopy-initiality packages.

Retains the constructors/recursion/dependent elimination/computation organization for one selected directed HIT, replacing loop paths by a directed generator and dependent paths by contextual coherence.
Retains recursive h-levels and closure ideas while distinguishing emdash truncation evidence and finite categorical height from an unimplemented truncation reflector or general truncation HIT.
Uses the question-first loop-space calculation as a rhetorical point of departure; all prose is newly written for the noninvertible WalkingEnd/Nat setting.
Retains the getting-started/model/cover/encode-decode progression while replacing paths and integers by directed arrows, natural powers, a contextual decoder, and directed normalization.
Compares constructor computation and loop powers with the selected directed HIT, explicitly removing inverse powers and predecessor cases.
Uses the generalize-the-endpoint and calculate-two-inverses proof pattern, with directed functor action replacing path transport.
Records the precise analogy and the points where invertibility, predecessor, univalence, and group cancellation do not transfer.
Adapts categories and precategories as a univalent 1-categorical specialization, with an explicit translation to native iterated Cat, equality-local structure, and finite categorical height.
Replaces pointwise-only naturality by off-diagonal tapp1 action, generic higher iteration, and a separate cut-calculus spiral in Chapter 9.
Leads with the checked unit/counit triangle cuts and then develops hom and profunctor representability as the mathematical reading of adjunction.
Separates ordinary categorical equivalence, fully-faithful/essentially-surjective data, strict category isomorphism, carrier equivalence, and native omega-equivalence evidence.
Connects the Yoneda lemma and representability to native representables, the unit profunctor, and the checked shaped co-Yoneda beta while retaining the full Cat-valued theorem boundary.
Preserves HoTT object-set strictness while separating it from strict transfor naturality and runtime rewrite strictness.
Develops dagger and unitary structure as additional free-form data and compares it carefully with, but does not identify it with, active opposite duality.
Presents a structure-over-carrier identity schema and identifies current evidence-property results as footholds rather than an implemented general structure identity principle.
Introduces Rezk completion by its universal property and compares the Yoneda-image and HIT/encode-decode routes without claiming an active native saturation construction.
Replaces a raw type-term first presentation by a readable categorical signature while keeping the full mathematical surface distinct from the bounded executable text subset.
Adapts explicit judgments, contexts, and formation/introduction/elimination/computation rules to the actual Lambdapi categorical encoding.
Replaces the circle-extension story by the book's qualified equality/univalence layers and selected directed WalkingEnd signature.
Retains the metatheory taxonomy while explicitly declining to transfer HoTT's conversion, normalization, canonicity, decidability, or consistency results to the emdash rewrite system without proof.

adaptations.description: Recasts the largest compact-open invertibility support as the representability question for the ordinary invertibility sieve D_U(s). The compact-open definition is retained as the correct coherent or qcqs specialization when a representing compact open exists; no emdash implementation of Zeuner's comparison theorem is claimed.

Adapts the functor-of-points, finite Zariski coverage, and localization-represented basic-open narrative while taking the ordinary sieve of invertibility probes as primary. A selected localization represents that sieve pointwise; a compact open or Zariski-lattice element is a further representation when available. The chapter does not import Zeuner's qcqs comparison theorem, compact-open classification, or general scheme theorem as an emdash result.

Adapts the finite affine-cover and global-versus-functorial scheme architecture to a global-first, site-relative presentation. Emdash starts with a supplied reflective ringed object and one covering sieve, selects two constructively generating affine realizations, and derives restrictions and a selected actual overlap from the single global structure presheaf. The chapter does not import an atlas-gluing theorem, a compact-open classifier, the functorial/local-ringed-lattice qcqs comparison, or a representation-independent category of schemes.

Carries the finite-affine-cover rhythm and explicit representation boundary into the supplied projective-line case. The Laurent-coordinate construction is read through actual principal-open restrictions and the sieve-first viewpoint, while the chapter states explicitly that Zeuner does not supply its projective-line or Proj construction. No atlas-gluing theorem, qcqs comparison, graded Proj, projective-space object, or non-affineness theorem is imported as an emdash result.
